paper.title_en: Black Hole Interiors as a Laboratory for Time-Dependent Classical Double Copy
paper.abstract_en: The classical double copy relates gravity and gauge theory, but its most explicit realizations remain concentrated in stationary or highly symmetric settings. We show that trapped regions of black-hole geometries provide an exact setting for time-dependent classical double copy. More generally, a class of Kantowski--Sachs cosmologies admits an intrinsic double-copy construction: the Kerr--Schild scalar and single-copy field are uniquely reconstructible from the cosmological metric alone, without prior knowledge that the spacetime is a black-hole interior or reference to any exterior completion. The reconstructed field admits both the standard flat-background Kerr--Schild realization and a complementary Maxwell realization on the Kantowski--Sachs geometry, where it describes a homogeneous, time-dependent electric field. We prove that this class is characterized by a relation between the Kantowski--Sachs scale factors equivalent to $p_{\parallel}=-ρ$. For Schwarzschild, the single-copy electric field diverges along the interior evolution, whereas for the regular Bardeen solution it remains finite throughout the trapped region and extends smoothly into the regular static core. The Bardeen geometry violates the strong energy condition in a compact central region, whereas the corresponding single-copy Maxwell field remains regular and satisfies the standard classical energy conditions. We further show that the Bardeen horizon phase structure is encoded in the single-copy scalar. Thus trapped Kerr--Schild interiors provide an exact local realization of time-dependent classical double copy.
